ch14-open.title: CAD drawings (DXF)
ch14-open.standfirst: Open a DXF drawing two ways — read it in place on the canvas, or open it in the docked CAD viewer with layers, fit and lock.

ch12-mental-model.eyebrow: How documents live on the canvas
ch12-mental-model.heading: Anchors, panes, and what your peers see
ch12-mental-model.lead: Every document you open started life as an upload in the room library — the bar on the right where files are grouped under PDF documents, CAD drawings, and IFC models. Dropping one onto the canvas creates an anchor: a tile that shows the document in place, sized and positioned like any other element.
ch12-mental-model.body: There are two ways to look at a document, and they behave differently. A PDF shows its page directly on the canvas inside the anchor — you read it where it sits. A DXF drawing or an IFC model can be explored right on the anchor too, or opened in a dedicated pane that docks to the right edge of the screen for a full interactive viewer with its own toolbar. The canvas anchor is the shared object; the pane is your personal workspace for inspecting it.
ch12-mental-model.pull: What you leave on the canvas — the page, the layers left showing, the angle you parked a model at — is shared with the room. The orbiting, slicing and measuring you do while exploring stays on your screen.

diagram.label: Library file → canvas anchor → docked viewer pane
diagram.cap: An uploaded file becomes a canvas anchor; DXF and IFC anchors can additionally open in a right-docked pane.

note.html: Canvas M accepts only four kinds of file. If someone tries to add anything else, the room reports “Only images, DXF, PDF and IFC are supported for now.” and skips it.

ch12-dxf-canvas.heading: Read a DXF without opening a pane
steps: Right-click a DXF anchor and choose Edit DXF (pan / zoom). The drawing comes alive in place — drag to pan, scroll to zoom.
Click 📋 Layers to open Layers (N). Every row carries the layer's own colour swatch; tick or untick to show or hide it, or use All and None to switch the lot.
↻ Fit reframes the whole drawing; × Exit (or Esc) leaves edit mode. Right-clicking also offers Reset fit (back to full view).
ch12-dxf-canvas.outcome: Unlike the CAD pane, a DXF edited here on the canvas is the shared object: the layers you hide and the view you leave are saved to the anchor and seen by everyone in the room.

note.html: Edit a DXF on the canvas when the whole room should see the change. Open the same drawing in the CAD view pane (next) when you want a big, private workspace — pane changes stay with you.

ch12-dxf-canvas.figcap: A DXF anchor in focus mode with the Layers panel, colour swatches, and the Fit / Exit toolbar.

ch12-cad-open.heading: Open a DXF in the CAD view
steps: Click the CAD view button in the canvas toolbar (the blueprint icon, tooltip “CAD view — open DXF in a pane”).
A popover titled DXF in library lists every drawing in the room. Pick one to open it as a tab in the right-docked pane.
Alternatively, right-click a DXF anchor on the canvas and choose Open in CAD view.
Each file opens in its own tab marked 📐; click a tab to switch, click its × to close just that drawing.
Drag the left edge of the pane (the resize handle) to make the viewer wider or narrower.
Close the whole pane with the × in the top-right corner.
ch12-cad-open.outcome: The DXF loads into an interactive viewer. Pan by dragging, zoom with the scroll wheel. Re-opening a drawing that is already a tab simply switches to it rather than duplicating.
ch12-cad-open.note: If the popover says “No DXF files in the library yet.” with the hint “Upload .dxf via the library bar on the right.”, there is simply nothing to open yet.
ch12-cad-open.figcap: A DXF open in the right-docked CAD view with the Layers, Fit, and Lock toolbar.

legend.text: Layers — opens the Layers (N) panel. Tick or untick each layer to show or hide it; the colour swatch matches the DXF layer colour. All turns everything on, None turns everything off.
Fit — resets the view to frame the whole drawing (tooltip “Fit DXF to pane (reset the view)”).
Lock / Locked — freezes pan and zoom so you cannot nudge the drawing by accident. Click again to unlock; the tooltip reads “View is locked — click to unlock pan/zoom” when active.
Tab strip — one tab per open drawing, each with a × to close it; the pane × at top-right closes the entire CAD view.

ch12-dxf-reference.heading: Every CAD-view control at a glance
rows: Pan and zoom the drawing right on the canvas anchor
Open the drawing in the right-docked pane
CAD view — open DXF in a pane
Show or hide individual layers; the swatch matches the layer colour
Fit DXF to pane (reset the view)
Freeze pan and zoom so the view can't be nudged
View is locked — click to unlock pan/zoom
One tab per drawing; × closes a tab, the pane × closes the viewer
ch12-dxf-reference.note: The CAD view is a 2D drawing viewer — it has no measure, snap, or unit tools (those belong to the 3D model view). And mind where a change lives: layers toggled in the pane are yours alone, while layers toggled on the canvas anchor are shared with the room.

ch12-trouble.heading: Document viewing — troubleshooting

rows.sym: A PDF / DXF / IFC tile shows “Waiting for … file from peer…”
rows.cause: The file bytes have not reached you yet — the person who added it is still syncing it across.
rows.fix: Wait a moment; it fills in automatically once the file arrives. No action needed.

rows.sym: A model sits in the library a few seconds before it will open
rows.cause: An IFC is converted to a lightweight 3D model when you upload it; bigger buildings take a little longer.
rows.fix: Wait for the conversion to finish — it only happens once, at upload.

rows.sym: “Maximum DXF files already open” (or “Maximum 3D models already open”)
rows.cause: Every live viewer slot is in use — heavy 3D models run at most two at once, DXF drawings up to four.
rows.fix: Close another open file or tab, then try opening this one again.

rows.sym: “Couldn't read DXF: …” or “Couldn't read IFC model: …”
rows.cause: The file is corrupt or in an unsupported variant; the message after the colon is the underlying reason.
rows.fix: Ask the owner to re-export and re-upload the file. (A .dwg won't open at all — it must be exported to .dxf.)

rows.sym: A DXF opens but all its text and dimensions are missing
rows.cause: The drawing relies on fonts the viewer doesn't have, so labels are dropped while the geometry still draws.
rows.fix: The lines are accurate; this is a display limit, not lost data. Re-export with standard fonts if the labels matter.

rows.sym: A DXF tab shows “DXF file not found”
rows.cause: The tab is left over from a different meeting; its file is not in this room's library.
rows.fix: Close the phantom tab — Canvas M also prunes these automatically once the library loads.

rows.sym: The 3D toolbar buttons are all greyed out
rows.cause: The model is still loading (“Loading 3D model…”) or has no storeys / objects to show.
rows.fix: Wait for the model to finish; tooltips like “No storeys” / “No objects” mean that data simply isn't in the file.

rows.sym: Page turns on a PDF have no effect
rows.cause: You are reviewing a finished meeting in read-only mode, where page changes are blocked.
rows.fix: This is expected — read-only review keeps the page fixed.

ch12-trouble.note: Pan, zoom, and orbit happen inside the viewer pane only — they never move the underlying canvas, so you can explore freely without disturbing the shared layout.
